correctness.rationale: For every \(b\ge2\), the restricted partition recurrence yields exact mod-two maps \(T_0,T_1,T_r\) on the adjacent shifted counting pair. Over the three nonzero \(\mathbb F_2\) states the transfer matrix has invariant \(x-y=1\) and exact level count \(H=1+y+z\). This gives \(H_b(k+1)=(b-1)H_b(k)+2H_b(k-1)-1\) with \(H_b(0)=1,H_b(1)=b\), its rational generating function and exact characteristic-root closed form. For \(b>2\), the positive root \(\lambda_b\) lies strictly between 1 and \(b\) and the negative root has absolute value at most one, yielding sharp \(\Theta_b(X^{\log_b\lambda_b})\) by power-bracketing. Known binary mod-three criterion proves density \(2/3\). Exact independent integer counts were replayed for bases two through eleven and full levels up to 175,000; finite checks are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The claimed advance is the exact b-uniform count of odd values on b-adic level sets and the corresponding sharp asymptotic support exponent. Underlying recurrences, binary congruence, individual-value formulas and pointwise growth bounds were already available and are excluded from priority. No inspected prior theorem states the same all-base aggregate law. Edgar 2018 has stronger pointwise coverage and Eom–Jeong–Sohn 2016 full text was not inspectable, so priority remains qualified; the explicit aggregate formula does not follow from prior quoted theorems without an additional transfer-matrix summation.
residual_risks: The Eom–Jeong–Sohn 2016 full text was not inspectable; its matrix method could implicitly include related parity aggregation.
Edgar 2018 covers all pointwise partition values, hence the aggregate can be recovered by summing, although the inspected work does not provide that formula.
Unindexed prior work or alternative automatic-sequence formulations may predate the explicit level generating function.

value.rationale: Parity prevalence is a motivated global invariant of the classical hyper-m-ary restricted partition functions. The exact rational level generating function classifies all bases and levels, including a sharp qualitative transition from natural density 2/3 at base two to density zero at every higher base; it also determines an exact nontrivial growth exponent in every sparse case. These are quantitative structure facts not a mere rephrasing of the known pointwise recurrence. The statement is fixed-base only, does not address higher congruence moduli or local fluctuations.
